SIMULATED proprietary social evidence — no live provider was called.
Observed audience-language patterns for one-person-company founders:
- They describe the pain as "I keep switching between selling, researching, following up, and actually doing the work."
- "AI manager" is often read as another dashboard or advisor unless the copy makes clear that work is actually carried through.
- The strongest desired outcome is one accountable system that can notice missing capability, get what it needs, do the work, and return with a finished result.
- Generic "automate your workflows" language feels broad and tool-like; concrete language about owning an outcome and finishing the job is easier to understand.
Recommended messaging implication: lead with the founder outcome and accountability, then explain the make-versus-buy capability underneath.

companyArtifacts.content:
Launch page — revised relaunch messaging package (draft for review; not published)

Status
Prepared for review only. This package revises the launch message to address the documented audience-recognition and signup-conversion problem. It does not claim improved performance until tested.

Evidence-backed context
- Intended audience: one-person-company founders and lean SME operators; the primary relaunch audience is one-person-company founders.
- Use context: a relaunch page intended to convert one-person-company founders.
- Diagnosis: current signup conversion is low, and visitors do not recognise themselves in the message.
- Product description: Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs.
Sources: company records, launch/context and company/profile.

Revised message hierarchy

1. Audience recognition
Eyebrow: For people building a company on their own

Headline: Run your one-person company with an AI manager by your side.

2. Core value proposition
Subhead: Somebody helps one-person-company founders keep the business moving by acting as an AI manager for the work that otherwise falls through the cracks.

3. Founder-relevant outcome
Supporting copy: Spend less time trying to manage every moving part yourself, and more time moving the company forward—with an AI manager built for the reality of running lean.

4. Product category and role
Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs. The message should explain the role plainly and avoid implying human staff, guaranteed outcomes, or capabilities not established in the supplied records.

5. Call to action
Primary CTA: See how Somebody can help run your one-person company
Secondary reassurance: Built for founders running lean; review the product details before signing up.

Connection to diagnosis
- The explicit “one-person company” language is intended to address the documented problem that visitors do not recognise themselves.
- The founder-specific framing and plain AI-manager category are intended to make the product’s relevance clear before signup.
- The revised message is a hypothesis for improving signup conversion, not evidence that conversion has improved.

Improvement criteria and test plan
Compare this package with the current message using comparable one-person-company-founder traffic and the same measurement window. Treat the package as directionally successful only if it improves:
- Signup conversion rate.
- Audience recognition: the share of visitors who identify the page as being for people like them.
- Message comprehension: the share who can accurately state who Somebody is for and what role it plays.
Record baseline, sample size, traffic mix, test dates, and results before deciding to publish. No performance threshold is supplied in the company records; the decision owner must set an approval threshold before the test.

Assumptions
- One-person-company founders are the intended primary audience for this relaunch.
- “AI manager” is an accurate, understandable product category for the supplied product description.
- The revised audience-specific wording will improve recognition and may improve signup conversion.
- Comparable founder traffic can be obtained without paid spend unless an explicit application-approved provider path is available.

Material risks and guardrails
- The benefit language (“keep the business moving,” “work that otherwise falls through the cracks,” and “spend less time”) is messaging hypothesis language and must not be treated as validated performance evidence.
- Avoid claims of guaranteed time savings, revenue growth, autonomous execution, human-equivalent support, or other capabilities not established by the supplied records.
- A stronger founder focus could reduce relevance for lean SMEs outside the primary audience; monitor audience mix and comprehension.
- The page remains a draft for review and must not be sent or published by this artifact change.

Unresolved dependencies
- Baseline signup conversion and a defined comparison window are not supplied here.
- No quantitative improvement threshold is supplied; a decision owner must define one.
- Test traffic comparability, sample size, and measurement instrumentation remain to be confirmed.
- Product capability details beyond the supplied “AI manager” description remain unverified.

Decision status
Review-ready for a relaunch test, not ready for an evidence-based claim of improved performance or for publication. Next decision: approve the test design and success threshold, run the comparison, review recognition, comprehension, and signup results, then decide whether to publish.

history.content:
Launch page — current message
Headline: "Somebody: an AI manager for your business."
Subhead: "Automate your workflows with AI."
Status: launch not converting; visitors leave without signing up.
Assumed audience: generic "businesses".
Assumed pain point: "too many tools".

Evidence-backed underperformance findings — draft for review (not published)

Affected audience
The relaunch is intended for one-person-company founders. Internal launch context reports low signup conversion and that visitors do not recognise themselves. [Source: company record, launch/context]

Principal messaging gaps and likely effects
1. Audience specificity gap: The current headline addresses "your business" and the artifact assumes generic "businesses," while the launch goal is to convert one-person-company founders. This mismatch is consistent with visitors not recognising themselves and is likely to reduce relevance and signup intent. The available evidence does not establish that it is the sole cause. [Source: company record, launch/context; current message above]
2. Outcome/accountability gap: "AI manager" can be read as another dashboard or advisor unless the message makes clear that work is carried through. The founder-language evidence describes a desired system that notices missing capability, gets what it needs, does the work, and returns with a finished result. Leaving execution and accountability implicit is likely to make the product sound advisory rather than outcome-owning. [Source: linked proprietary-data acquisition, resultEvidenceId sim_result_d355d8ca39e49d9ae0264ace]
3. Broad/tool-like wording: "Automate your workflows with AI" is generic and does not state whose work is completed or what result the founder receives. Founder-language evidence says generic workflow-automation language feels broad and tool-like, while concrete language about owning an outcome and finishing the job is easier to understand. This likely weakens comprehension and differentiation, contributing to lower signup intent. [Source: linked proprietary-data acquisition, resultEvidenceId sim_result_d355d8ca39e49d9ae0264ace]
4. Pain-point contradiction: The current artifact assumes "too many tools," but the observed founder language emphasizes switching between selling, researching, following up, and doing the work. The current pain framing may therefore fail to mirror the more specific workload fragmentation founders describe, reducing recognition. [Source: linked proprietary-data acquisition, resultEvidenceId sim_result_d355d8ca39e49d9ae0264ace]

Messaging direction to test
Lead with the one-person-company founder outcome and accountability: a system that owns a task through completion and returns with a finished result. Explain the make-versus-buy capability underneath, rather than leading with the abstract label "AI manager" or generic workflow automation. This is a test direction, not a claim of proven causal lift. [Source: linked proprietary-data acquisition, resultEvidenceId sim_result_d355d8ca39e49d9ae0264ace]

Criteria for judging improvement
- Primary: signup conversion improves versus the current launch baseline, measured on comparable traffic and page conditions.
- Recognition: in a short visitor survey or interview, more target one-person-company founders identify the page as relevant to them and accurately describe the job Somebody completes.
- Message comprehension: target visitors can state that Somebody carries work through to a finished result, rather than merely advising or providing another dashboard.
- Diagnostic comparison: compare the revised outcome/accountability-led message with the current message using the same audience and measurement window; interpret results cautiously because the existing evidence does not isolate one causal factor.

Status
Prepared for review only. This package revises the launch message to address the documented audience-recognition and signup-conversion problem. It does not claim improved performance until tested.

Evidence-backed context
- The relaunch goal is to convert one-person-company founders.
- Current signal: low signup conversion; visitors do not recognise themselves.
- Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs.
Sources: company records, launch/context and company/profile.

Revised message hierarchy

1. Audience recognition
Eyebrow: For people building a company on their own

Headline: Run your one-person company with an AI manager by your side.

2. Core value proposition
Subhead: Somebody helps one-person-company founders keep the business moving by acting as an AI manager for the work that otherwise falls through the cracks.

3. Founder-relevant outcome
Supporting copy: Spend less time trying to manage every moving part yourself, and more time moving the company forward—with an AI manager built for the reality of running lean.

4. Product category and role
Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs. It is intended to extend what a founder can do; this page does not claim specific automations, integrations, time savings, revenue gains, or guaranteed results that are not substantiated by the supplied records.

5. Call to action
Primary CTA: Meet your AI manager
Secondary reassurance: Built for one-person companies and lean teams.

Suggested page copy

For people building a company on their own
Run your one-person company with an AI manager by your side.

Somebody helps one-person-company founders keep the business moving by acting as an AI manager for the work that otherwise falls through the cracks.

You do not need a bigger team to operate with more leverage. Somebody is built for one-person companies and lean SMEs, extending what a founder can do while they run the business.

[Meet your AI manager]

Why this message is different
- It names the intended audience directly instead of addressing generic “businesses.”
- It leads with the founder’s operating reality and desired leverage rather than the vague instruction to “automate your workflows.”
- It explains the product category (“AI manager”) in relation to the founder’s work without inventing unsupported capabilities.
- It uses one clear value proposition and a single primary action.

Claim substantiation and guardrails
- “Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs.” Source: company record, company/profile.
- “The relaunch is intended to convert one-person-company founders; current signal is low signup conversion and visitors do not recognise themselves.” Source: company record, launch/context.
- “Helps … keep the business moving,” “work that otherwise falls through the cracks,” “more leverage,” and “by your side” are positioning language for review, not measured performance claims. Validate them before treating them as substantiated outcomes.
- Do not add quantified benefits, named workflows, integrations, customer results, or guarantees without supporting evidence.

Diagnosis addressed
1. Audience specificity gap: replaced generic “your business” framing with “one-person-company founders” and “one-person companies.”
2. Outcome/accountability gap: retained the supported “AI manager” category while clarifying its role as support for the founder’s work; avoided unsupported operational promises.
3. Generic workflow language: replaced “Automate your workflows with AI” with founder-relevant language about running a lean company and extending founder capacity.
4. Message hierarchy gap: ordered the page as audience → value proposition → founder-relevant outcome → product role → CTA.

Current message preserved for comparison
Headline: “Somebody: an AI manager for your business.”
Subhead: “Automate your workflows with AI.”
Status: launch not converting; visitors leave without signing up.
Assumed audience: generic “businesses.”
Assumed pain point: “too many tools.”

Testing note
Review and test this package against the current message with comparable one-person-company-founder traffic. Measure signup conversion, audience recognition, and message comprehension before publishing a winning variant.

Source records
- company/profile — company profile
- launch/context — launch context and goals

The prerequisite req_01 is satisfied, and the available evidence supports diagnosing a mismatch between the generic current message and the audience’s stronger need for an accountable system that completes work. The option also passed checks for owned inputs, governed primitives, available proof, and worker availability, with no open external resource needs.

Select the eligible internal MAKE option. It has the required governed primitives, owned inputs, available worker, and proof capability to create and save the relaunch messaging package. The satisfied req_02 diagnosis identifies the target audience as one-person-company founders and documents specific gaps in audience relevance, outcome/accountability, and message clarity, providing a direct basis for a coherent value proposition, audience-relevant hierarchy, and substantiated claims. Select the internal MAKE option because it is the only legally eligible option and its available capabilities—company-record lookup and document drafting—fit the requirement for a decision-ready relaunch messaging brief. The prerequisite req_03 is satisfied, the required inputs and governing primitives are available, proof is available, and a worker is available. The existing controlled draft already addresses the diagnosed audience-recognition and signup-conversion problem, identifies the intended audience and use context, preserves traceability to company and launch records, and includes claim guardrails.
